# Round 32 of the relation-map review

Previous rounds: `audit_evidence_claims/m1` to `m31` (`REPORT.md`; m27 and m29 stopped early, so their `attacks/` folders are the record). All repairs are in `CODEX_MAP_M1_VERDICT.md`. Review the latest commit on HEAD. Run the tests with `python -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider`; expect 361. Start the page with `python src/app.py <port>` on a port other than 8765 and exercise it over HTTP.

## What changed since round 31: a design change, not another word-list repair

Rounds 20 to 31 each found new wording that the question linker's product markers did not cover. The relation map no longer depends on those markers. See the section "Before round 32" in `CODEX_MAP_M1_VERDICT.md`, and `src/app.py` `Engine.explore`, `_sig`, `_latin`.

- **P32-1.** `explore` draws only when the whole input is one name. The linker must read exactly one entity, and its matched text must have the same letters, digits and symbols as the input (`_sig`: NFKC, casefold, any script). Case, spaces, punctuation and ®/™/© do not count. Anything else returns `not_one_name`, and the page asks for the name alone.
- **P32-2.** If any part of the input is refused, the whole input is refused.
- **P32-3.** A name stored for several live nodes is not drawn. The reply is `choose`: the nodes are listed and the reader clicks one, which loads it by id.
- **P32-4.** Lower-case `nct`/`chembl`/`ensg` ids are read. The whole input can be a company key or target name when `_latin(text)` equals the dictionary key, so a symbol the key would drop still blocks it (for example "Merck & Co").
- **P32-5.** This change is in the question linker, `src/query.py` `_whole_name` and the end of `_link`. A canonical key shared by several drugs is no longer decided by its spelling; only a drug's own preferred name chooses it. Inside such a key, a shorter name is not read either. Before, "medi4736" read as atezolizumab and "5-fluorouracil" as capecitabine.
- **New tests:** `tests/test_app.py::test_the_map_draws_only_a_whole_stored_name` and `test_a_key_shared_by_several_drugs_is_not_decided_by_spelling`. Older map tests that drew a centre from a longer input now go through `_page`: the map must not draw, and the question linker's reading is checked instead.
- **Docs:** README defect 15 (both languages) records that the question boxes still rely on the linker's markers for free text. Defect 9 records the shared keys. Section 0 of `web/try.html` states the one-name rule.

## Scope and approval bar

The subject is the relation map: section 0 of `web/try.html`, `POST /api/explore`, `Engine.explore`. The guarantees are those in the original brief below, with guarantee 3 now read as follows: the map draws a node only for an input that is, as a whole, one stored name of that node (or its id). It never draws a refused product, tracer or conjugate as the originator, and never draws one of several nodes that share a name.

1. Re-run every earlier reproduction from m1 to m31 against the map, and mark each finding FIXED or NOT FIXED. Reuse the earlier scripts. Inputs that were longer than a name should now be refused, `not_one_name`, `choose` or `not_found`, never a drawn originator.
2. Attack the new rule:
   - any input that draws a node the input does not name as a whole
   - a whole stored name that is in fact a different product (a data problem; say so, and separate it from code problems)
   - Unicode, symbols and invisible characters that `_sig`/`_latin` mishandle
   - the id path
   - the `choose` reply (live nodes only, injection-safe page markup, click-through)
   - company/target whole-name reads
   - retired nodes
   - anything the page text claims that the code does not do
3. Check P32-5 for regressions in the question boxes (2 to 4) and the demo examples. Report over-refusals as should-fix, not blockers.
4. Re-check guarantees A to G of the original brief briefly; earlier rounds approved them.

### Out of scope as blockers (recorded)

- The question boxes' free-text refusal relies on word lists (README defect 15). A leak there is a note, not a map blocker.
- Known data limitations, awaiting the owner's curation decision:
  - ChEMBL lists bevacizumab biosimilar development codes as bevacizumab synonyms.
  - An AACT synonym maps 13-cis-retinoic acid to CHEMBL38 tretinoin (M23-D1).
  - "Roche" is stored as a folic acid alias. The map now asks the reader to choose.
- Known over-refusals listed in `CODEX_MAP_M1_VERDICT.md` (M5-S2, rapamycin forms, Trastuzumab--vcmmae conjugate, 9-amino-20(s)-camptothecin, il-6ra, TAK-659F, GS-11CAL-101, 3en3hg4wsw, an ADC named with its own payload beside it). A longer input not being drawn is the new rule, not an over-refusal.

Approval bar: no known way for the map to draw a node for an input that is not, as a whole, one stored name or id of it. That includes a refused product drawn as the originator, one of several same-named nodes drawn without the reader's choice, a wrong relation or direction, a value that differs from the stored one, and script injection. Report should-fix items separately from blockers.

---
name: review
description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes ??Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/PRD asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
---

Two-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:

- **Standards** ??does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?
- **Spec** ??does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / PRD / spec?

Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.

The issue tracker should have been provided to you ??run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing.

## Process

### 1. Pin the fixed point

Whatever the user said is the fixed point ??a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc. If they didn't specify one, ask for it.

Capture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.

Before going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here ??not inside two parallel sub-agents.

### 2. Identify the spec source

Look for the originating spec, in this order:

1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.) ??fetch via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
2. A path the user passed as an argument.
3. A PRD/spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.
4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report "no spec available".

### 3. Identify the standards sources

Anything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel

Send a single message with two `Agent` tool calls. Use the `general-purpose` subagent for both.

**Standards sub-agent prompt** ??include:

- The full diff command and commit list.
- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3.
- The brief: "Report ??per file/hunk where relevant ??every place the diff violates a documented standard. Cite the standard (file + the rule). Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words."

**Spec sub-agent prompt** ??include:

- The diff command and commit list.
- The path or fetched contents of the spec.
- The brief: "Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words."

If the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.

### 5. Aggregate

Present the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings ??the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).

End with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes ??that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.

## Why two axes

A change can pass one axis and fail the other:

- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing ??**Standards pass, Spec fail.**
- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions ??**Spec pass, Standards fail.**

Reporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.

## The guarantees claimed (page text in section 0 and the `explore` docstring)

1. Every neighbour shown is joined to the centre by a live (not retired) edge to a live node, and the group label
   states the relation and its direction correctly (e.g. "???쎌쓽 ?꾩긽??二쇨???怨?(二쇨? ??媛쒕컻)" for
   Company -SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF-> Drug seen from the drug).
2. Details shown for a neighbour are the stored values: trial phases/status/start/title/url, sponsor trial count
   (`evidence_trials`) and sponsor class, drug trial count in the graph (EVALUATES), max phase, action type.
3. A name the question linker refuses (biosimilar, distinct product, tracer) is reported as refused, never drawn
   as the originator molecule; an unknown name says "not found".
4. Groups are ordered by size and each list keeps the `per_group` neighbours with most evidence; the page says
   when a list is cut and shows the true total.
5. Nothing is written; no model is called.

## What to verify (reproduce; cite file:line and exact inputs)

A. **Wrong relations or directions.** Any centre where an edge is grouped under the wrong label or direction,
   self-loops (src == dst), edges with both ends equal to the centre, PARENT_OF/SPONSORS/STUDIES/ASSOCIATED_WITH
   direction wording, Investigator vs Company handling, nodes whose type the tables do not cover.
B. **Name resolution.** `explore` takes the first non-refused hit of `link_entities`. Inputs with several entities
   ("osimertinib EGFR"), a refused token next to a real one ("Mvasi bevacizumab"), salts vs parents, company aliases
   with `also_matching_ids` (only the first id is drawn ??is that misleading?), node ids vs names that collide,
   case/whitespace/Unicode, long inputs. Is anything drawn that the input does not name, or a refused product drawn
   as the originator?
C. **Wrong values.** Trial counts, sponsor counts, max phase and action shown versus the database
   (`data/processed/oncokg.sqlite`); retired edges/nodes leaking in; counts computed over retired edges;
   the `trials` count chunking; JSON props that are null or malformed.
D. **Cutting and ordering.** Is the "most evidence" ordering what the page says (trials are ordered by start date
   string ??is that what the text implies)? Does the map's subset (`drawMap` allocation) ever hide a whole group
   or misstate totals? The Disease node (thousands of neighbours) ??performance and output size.
E. **Page safety and correctness.** HTML/SVG injection from labels, titles, ids, URLs (`href` with `javascript:`?),
   edge ids in `data-id` attributes, the trail/back buttons after errors, double clicks, refused/not-found states,
   dark mode legibility is not in scope.
F. **Server.** Error handling for empty/oversized input, concurrency with the lock, behaviour when the DB has
   retired rows.
G. **Docs and wording.** Section 0 text, README/README.ko lines for `app.py`, the module docstring: do they claim
   more than the code does? Korean labels in GKO/ACT/PH that misstate the stored code.

web/try.html
"""A local page for trying the pipeline by hand.

    python src/app.py            then open http://localhost:8765

A relation map (a node and the nodes live edges tie it to, a capped list per relation,
click to move on),
then four boxes: type an intervention string the way a registry would write it and see
how the resolver reads it, or ask a question and see the grounded answer with its
evidence, give a structured answer (claims citing evidence edges) and see which
claims the graph supports and the answer written from them, or paste free prose and
see what the auxiliary word-order check flags. All of them call
the functions the pipeline uses (resolve_drug_string, OncoKG.answer,
OncoKG.check_groundedness) on the built artefacts, so what the page shows is what the
pipeline would do. Nothing is written; the language model is never called.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import sqlite3
import sys
import threading
import unicodedata
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import config as C
import normalize as N
import textrules as T
from query import OncoKG

PAGE = C.WEB / "try.html"
PORT = 8765


class Engine:
    def __init__(self):
        self.kg = OncoKG()
        # A browser opens spare connections it may never use, which would stall a
        # single-threaded server; requests are threaded, the engine is not.
        self.kg.conn.close()
        self.kg.conn = sqlite3.connect(C.PROCESSED / "oncokg.sqlite", check_same_thread=False)
        self.kg.conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.dic = self.kg.dic
        self.index_keys = self.kg.index_keys
        target_rows, _, _ = N._load("targets")
        self.target_keys = N.target_guard_keys(target_rows, self.dic)
        # every node by its own label, so a name the graph itself shows can be typed back
        self.by_label: dict = {}
        for r in self.kg.conn.execute("SELECT id, label FROM node"):
            if r["label"]:
                self.by_label.setdefault(_label_key(r["label"]), []).append(r["id"])

    def resolve(self, text: str) -> dict:
        out = N.resolve_drug_string(text, self.dic, self.index_keys, self.target_keys)
        for c in out["components"]:
            d = self.dic["drugs"].get(c.get("drug_id") or "")
            if d:
                c["drug"] = {k: d.get(k) for k in
                             ("name", "drug_type", "max_phase_overall", "max_phase_in_nsclc")}
                c["drug"]["mechanisms"] = [m.get("mechanismOfAction") if isinstance(m, dict) else m
                                           for m in (d.get("mechanisms") or [])][:3]
                c["drug"]["trials"] = self.kg.conn.execute(
                    "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM edge WHERE rel='EVALUATES' AND dst=? AND retired_at IS NULL",
                    (d["drug_id"],)).fetchone()[0]
                par = self.dic["drugs"].get(d.get("parent_molecule") or "")
                if par:
                    c["drug"]["parent"] = {"name": par["name"], "trials": self.kg.conn.execute(
                        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM edge WHERE rel='EVALUATES' AND dst=? AND retired_at IS NULL",
                        (par["drug_id"],)).fetchone()[0]}
            if c.get("candidates"):
                c["candidate_names"] = [
                    (self.dic["drugs"].get(x) or {}).get("name", x) for x in c["candidates"]]
        return out

    def explore(self, text: str, per_group: int = 30) -> dict:
        """One live node and the live nodes its live edges tie it to, grouped by relation.

        `text` is a node id, a node's own label, or one name: the whole input (case,
        spaces, punctuation and trademark signs aside) must be the one name the question
        linker read, written in Latin letters and ASCII digits and symbols (`_plain`).
        Anything more (a second name, a qualifier, a payload, a dye, a sentence) is not
        drawn, because a word the linker does not know may make the name a different
        product; the reply says to enter the name alone. A name the linker refuses (a
        biosimilar, a reformulation, a tracer) is reported, never mapped to the
        originator. A name that is stored for several nodes is not drawn either: the
        nodes are listed and the reader picks one by its id.

        Each group keeps `per_group` neighbours, sorted as the page states: trials by
        start date (latest first), drugs by trials in the graph, sponsors by trials they
        lead, disease targets by association score. Sponsorship keeps its role (lead
        sponsor or collaborator)."""
        conn = self.kg.conn
        matched = None
        ref = text.strip()
        if re.fullmatch(r"(?i)(nct|chembl|ensg)\d+", ref):
            ref = ref.upper()                         # an id typed in lower case
        row = conn.execute("SELECT id FROM node WHERE id=? AND retired_at IS NULL",
                           (ref,)).fetchone()
        if row:
            nid = row["id"]
        else:
            ents = self.kg.link_entities(text)
            refused = [e for e in ents if e["type"] == "Refused"]
            hits = [e for e in ents if e.get("id") and e["type"] != "Refused"]
            if refused:                       # any refused part: the input is not one plain name
                return {"refused": refused[0]["label"], "why": refused[0]["why"]}
            ids = []
            whole = (len(hits) == 1 and _plain(text) and bool(_sig(text))
                     and _sig(hits[0].get("matched_text") or "") == _sig(text))
            if whole:
                matched = hits[0].get("matched_alias") or hits[0].get("matched_text")
                ids += [hits[0]["id"]] + list(hits[0].get("also_matching_ids") or [])
            # the whole input may also be a node's own label, or an organisation or a
            # target the linker passed over or split ("Roche" is also a folic acid alias,
            # "Merck & Co" is cut at "&", "MAGEA3" is also a vaccine alias)
            ids += self.by_label.get(_label_key(text), [])
            key = T.canonical_key(text)
            if key and _plain(text):
                ids += self.kg.companies.get(key, [])
            t = self.kg.targets.get(text.strip().lower())
            if t:
                ids.append(t["target_id"])
            choices = []
            for oid in ids:
                lab = conn.execute("SELECT type, label FROM node WHERE id=? AND retired_at IS NULL",
                                   (oid,)).fetchone()
                if lab and all(c["id"] != oid for c in choices):
                    choices.append({"id": oid, "type": lab["type"], "label": lab["label"]})
            if not choices:                   # nothing live by that name, or more than a name
                return {"not_one_name": text} if hits and not whole else {"not_found": text}
            if len(choices) > 1:
                # one name, several nodes ("Roche"): none is drawn in place of the others;
                # the reader picks one by its id
                return {"choose": choices, "text": text}
            nid = choices[0]["id"]
        node = conn.execute("SELECT id, type, label, props FROM node WHERE id=? "
                            "AND retired_at IS NULL", (nid,)).fetchone()
        if node is None:                              # a name can outlive its node
            return {"not_found": text}
        rows = conn.execute(
            "SELECT e.id AS eid, e.rel, e.src, e.props AS eprops, n.id, n.type, n.label, "
            "n.props AS nprops FROM edge e JOIN node n "
            "ON n.id = CASE WHEN e.src=? THEN e.dst ELSE e.src END "
            "WHERE (e.src=? OR e.dst=?) AND e.retired_at IS NULL AND n.retired_at IS NULL",
            (nid, nid, nid)).fetchall()
        drug_ids = list({r["id"] for r in rows if r["type"] == "Drug"} | {nid})
        trials = {}
        for i in range(0, len(drug_ids), 500):
            chunk = drug_ids[i:i + 500]
            trials.update(conn.execute(               # live trials only
                "SELECT e.dst, COUNT(*) FROM edge e JOIN node t ON t.id = e.src "
                "WHERE e.rel='EVALUATES' AND e.retired_at IS NULL AND t.retired_at IS NULL "
                f"AND e.dst IN ({','.join('?' * len(chunk))}) GROUP BY e.dst", chunk).fetchall())
        groups: dict = {}
        for r in rows:
            ep, np_ = _obj(r["eprops"]), _obj(r["nprops"])
            item = {"id": r["id"], "type": r["type"], "label": r["label"], "edge_id": r["eid"]}
            role = ep.get("role") if r["rel"] == "SPONSORS" else None
            if r["type"] == "Drug":
                item["trials"] = trials.get(r["id"], 0)
                item["max_phase"] = np_.get("max_phase_overall")
            if r["rel"] == "SPONSORS_TRIAL_OF":
                n = ep.get("evidence_trials")
                # a count the edge does not record stays unknown; 0 is only for sorting
                item["evidence_trials"] = n if _number(n) else None
                item["weight"] = n if _number(n) else 0
                item["sponsor_class"] = ep.get("sponsor_class")
            elif r["type"] == "Trial":
                item.update({k: np_.get(k) for k in ("phases", "status", "title", "start_date", "url")})
                item["weight"] = str(np_.get("start_date") or "")
            elif r["type"] == "Drug":
                item["weight"] = item["trials"]
            elif r["rel"] == "ASSOCIATED_WITH":
                score = ep.get("association_score")
                item["score"] = score if _number(score) else None
                item["weight"] = item["score"] or 0
            else:
                item["weight"] = 0
            if r["rel"] == "ACTS_ON":
                item["action"] = ep.get("action_type")
            if role:
                item["role"] = role
            key = (r["rel"], "out" if r["src"] == nid else "in", r["type"], role)
            groups.setdefault(key, []).append(item)
        out = []
        for (rel, direction, ntype, role), items in groups.items():
            items.sort(key=lambda x: x["label"] or "")              # names A to Z
            items.sort(key=lambda x: x["weight"], reverse=True)     # then by the stated weight
            out.append({"rel": rel, "dir": direction, "type": ntype, "role": role,
                        "total": len(items), "items": items[:per_group]})
        out.sort(key=lambda g: -g["total"])
        props = _obj(node["props"])
        return {"center": {"id": node["id"], "type": node["type"], "label": node["label"],
                           "matched_text": matched,
                           "trials": trials.get(node["id"], 0) if node["type"] == "Drug" else None,
                           "props": {k: props.get(k) for k in
                                     ("max_phase_overall", "drug_type", "phases", "status",
                                      "title", "url", "start_date") if props.get(k) is not None}},
                "groups": out}

    def ask(self, question: str) -> dict:
        return self.kg.answer(question, use_llm=False).to_dict()

    def structured(self, question: str, payload: str) -> dict:
        """Check a structured answer (claims citing edges) and write the answer from it."""
        kg = self.kg
        entities = kg.link_entities(question)
        evidence = kg.retrieve(kg.classify(question, entities), entities)
        res = kg.verify_structured(payload, evidence)
        res["evidence"] = [{"edge_id": e.edge_id, "statement": e.statement} for e in evidence]
        return res

    def check(self, question: str, answer: str) -> dict:
        """Check an answer someone else wrote against the evidence for the question."""
        kg = self.kg
        entities = kg.link_entities(question)
        intent = kg.classify(question, entities)
        evidence = kg.retrieve(intent, entities)
        checks = kg.check_groundedness(answer, evidence, entities, generated=True,
                                       vocabulary=set(self.dic["index"]),
                                       linker=kg.link_entities)
        return {"intent": intent, "entities": entities, "checks": checks,
                "evidence": [{"statement": e.statement, "source_record": e.source_record,
                              "source": e.source, "url": e.url} for e in evidence[:8]],
                "evidence_count": len(evidence)}


_MARKS = "®™©℠"          # registered, trade mark, copyright, service mark


def _sig(text: str) -> str:
    """The letters, digits and symbols of a name without case, spaces, punctuation or
    trademark signs: what must match between the input and the name the linker read."""
    t = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text or "").casefold()
    return "".join(c for c in t
                   if unicodedata.category(c)[0] not in "PZC" and c not in _MARKS)


def _label_key(text: str) -> str:
    """A node label as typed: compatibility forms folded, case and spacing ignored."""
    return " ".join(unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text or "").casefold().split())


def _plain(text: str) -> bool:
    """Every character is one the dictionary key may safely drop or keeps: Latin letters
    (accents allowed), ASCII digits, punctuation, ASCII symbols, trademark signs, spaces
    and invisible characters. A Greek letter, another script, a non-ASCII symbol or digit
    is dropped by the key yet can change the meaning (interferon followed by a Greek
    gamma, a radiation sign inside "trastuzumab"), so such input is never read as a
    stored name."""
    for c in unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text or ""):
        cat = unicodedata.category(c)
        if cat[0] in "PZCM" or c in _MARKS or (c.isascii() and cat[0] in "SN"):
            continue
        if cat[0] == "L" and unicodedata.name(c, "").startswith("LATIN "):
            continue
        return False
    return True


def _number(v) -> bool:
    return isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool) and v == v


def _obj(raw) -> dict:
    """Stored props as a dict; anything else (null, a list, broken JSON) as empty."""
    try:
        v = json.loads(raw) if raw else {}
    except ValueError:
        return {}
    return v if isinstance(v, dict) else {}


def make_handler(engine: Engine):
    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def _send(self, code: int, body: bytes, ctype: str):
            self.send_response(code)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", ctype)
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body)

        def do_GET(self):
            if self.path in ("/", "/index.html"):
                self._send(200, PAGE.read_bytes(), "text/html; charset=utf-8")
            else:
                self._send(404, b"not found", "text/plain")

        def do_POST(self):
            try:
                n = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
                body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(min(n, 20000)) or b"{}")
                text = str(body.get("text") or "").strip()
                if len(text) > 500:                      # refused, not silently cut
                    raise ValueError("input is longer than 500 characters")
                if not text:
                    raise ValueError("empty input")
                if self.path not in ("/api/resolve", "/api/ask", "/api/check",
                                     "/api/structured", "/api/explore"):
                    return self._send(404, b"{}", "application/json")
                with engine.lock:
                    if self.path == "/api/explore":
                        res = engine.explore(text)
                    elif self.path == "/api/resolve":
                        res = engine.resolve(text)
                    elif self.path == "/api/ask":
                        res = engine.ask(text)
                    elif self.path == "/api/structured":
                        answer = str(body.get("answer") or "").strip()[:20000]
                        if not answer:
                            raise ValueError("empty answer")
                        res = engine.structured(text, answer)
                    else:
                        answer = str(body.get("answer") or "").strip()[:4000]
                        if not answer:
                            raise ValueError("empty answer")
                        res = engine.check(text, answer)
                self._send(200, json.dumps(res, ensure_ascii=False,
                                           allow_nan=False).encode("utf-8"),
                           "application/json; charset=utf-8")
            except Exception as e:  # show the reason on the page, not a dead request
                self._send(400, json.dumps({"error": str(e)}, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8"),
                           "application/json; charset=utf-8")

        def log_message(self, *a):
            pass
    return Handler


def main() -> None:
    port = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else PORT
    engine = Engine()
    print(f"OncoKG try-it page: http://localhost:{port}", flush=True)
    ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), make_handler(engine)).serve_forever()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

---BRIEF---
# Round 32 of the relation-map review

Previous rounds: `audit_evidence_claims/m1` to `m31` (`REPORT.md`; m27 and m29 stopped early, so their `attacks/` folders are the record). All repairs are in `CODEX_MAP_M1_VERDICT.md`. Review the latest commit on HEAD. Run the tests with `python -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider`; expect 361. Start the page with `python src/app.py <port>` on a port other than 8765 and exercise it over HTTP.

## What changed since round 31: a design change, not another word-list repair

Rounds 20 to 31 each found new wording that the question linker's product markers did not cover. The relation map no longer depends on those markers. See the section "Before round 32" in `CODEX_MAP_M1_VERDICT.md`, and `src/app.py` `Engine.explore`, `_sig`, `_latin`.

- **P32-1.** `explore` draws only when the whole input is one name. The linker must read exactly one entity, and its matched text must have the same letters, digits and symbols as the input (`_sig`: NFKC, casefold, any script). Case, spaces, punctuation and ®/™/© do not count. Anything else returns `not_one_name`, and the page asks for the name alone.
- **P32-2.** If any part of the input is refused, the whole input is refused.
- **P32-3.** A name stored for several live nodes is not drawn. The reply is `choose`: the nodes are listed and the reader clicks one, which loads it by id.
- **P32-4.** Lower-case `nct`/`chembl`/`ensg` ids are read. The whole input can be a company key or target name when `_latin(text)` equals the dictionary key, so a symbol the key would drop still blocks it (for example "Merck & Co").
- **P32-5.** This change is in the question linker, `src/query.py` `_whole_name` and the end of `_link`. A canonical key shared by several drugs is no longer decided by its spelling; only a drug's own preferred name chooses it. Inside such a key, a shorter name is not read either. Before, "medi4736" read as atezolizumab and "5-fluorouracil" as capecitabine.
- **New tests:** `tests/test_app.py::test_the_map_draws_only_a_whole_stored_name` and `test_a_key_shared_by_several_drugs_is_not_decided_by_spelling`. Older map tests that drew a centre from a longer input now go through `_page`: the map must not draw, and the question linker's reading is checked instead.
- **Docs:** README defect 15 (both languages) records that the question boxes still rely on the linker's markers for free text. Defect 9 records the shared keys. Section 0 of `web/try.html` states the one-name rule.

## Scope and approval bar

The subject is the relation map: section 0 of `web/try.html`, `POST /api/explore`, `Engine.explore`. The guarantees are those in the original brief below, with guarantee 3 now read as follows: the map draws a node only for an input that is, as a whole, one stored name of that node (or its id). It never draws a refused product, tracer or conjugate as the originator, and never draws one of several nodes that share a name.

1. Re-run every earlier reproduction from m1 to m31 against the map, and mark each finding FIXED or NOT FIXED. Reuse the earlier scripts. Inputs that were longer than a name should now be refused, `not_one_name`, `choose` or `not_found`, never a drawn originator.
2. Attack the new rule:
   - any input that draws a node the input does not name as a whole
   - a whole stored name that is in fact a different product (a data problem; say so, and separate it from code problems)
   - Unicode, symbols and invisible characters that `_sig`/`_latin` mishandle
   - the id path
   - the `choose` reply (live nodes only, injection-safe page markup, click-through)
   - company/target whole-name reads
   - retired nodes
   - anything the page text claims that the code does not do
3. Check P32-5 for regressions in the question boxes (2 to 4) and the demo examples. Report over-refusals as should-fix, not blockers.
4. Re-check guarantees A to G of the original brief briefly; earlier rounds approved them.

### Out of scope as blockers (recorded)

- The question boxes' free-text refusal relies on word lists (README defect 15). A leak there is a note, not a map blocker.
- Known data limitations, awaiting the owner's curation decision:
  - ChEMBL lists bevacizumab biosimilar development codes as bevacizumab synonyms.
  - An AACT synonym maps 13-cis-retinoic acid to CHEMBL38 tretinoin (M23-D1).
  - "Roche" is stored as a folic acid alias. The map now asks the reader to choose.
- Known over-refusals listed in `CODEX_MAP_M1_VERDICT.md` (M5-S2, rapamycin forms, Trastuzumab--vcmmae conjugate, 9-amino-20(s)-camptothecin, il-6ra, TAK-659F, GS-11CAL-101, 3en3hg4wsw, an ADC named with its own payload beside it). A longer input not being drawn is the new rule, not an over-refusal.

Approval bar: no known way for the map to draw a node for an input that is not, as a whole, one stored name or id of it. That includes a refused product drawn as the originator, one of several same-named nodes drawn without the reader's choice, a wrong relation or direction, a value that differs from the stored one, and script injection. Report should-fix items separately from blockers.

Write scratch files only under `audit_evidence_claims/m32/`. Put the report in `audit_evidence_claims/m32/REPORT.md`. Do not edit tracked files. End with exactly one line: `VERDICT: APPROVE` or `VERDICT: CHANGES REQUIRED`.

+def _sig(text: str) -> str:
+    """The letters, digits and symbols of a name without case, spaces, punctuation or
+    trademark signs: what must match between the input and the name the linker read."""

+def _plain(text: str) -> bool:
+    """Every character is one the dictionary key may safely drop or keeps: Latin letters
+    (accents allowed), ASCII digits, punctuation, ASCII symbols, trademark signs, spaces
+    and invisible characters. A Greek letter, another script, a non-ASCII symbol or digit
+    is dropped by the key yet can change the meaning (interferon followed by a Greek

## M31-B1 — a setting/site preposition hides an explicit additional conjugation partner (P1)

**Inherited ordinary-drug primary:** `trastuzumab linked at lysine residues to eFluor 450` returns **TRASTUZUMAB / CHEMBL1201585**, the exact bare-trastuzumab map (**13 graph trials**) and complete trial/sponsor evidence (**12 / 12 rows**). **New-regression primary:** `trastuzumab emtansine conjugated at lysine residues to eFluor 450` returns **TRASTUZUMAB EMTANSINE / CHEMBL1743082**, its exact bare map and evidence (**5 / 5 / 5** graph/trial-QA/sponsor-QA). HEAD^ query.py refuses the latter and supplies **0 / 0** QA evidence. The deruxtecan counterpart changes from refusal to **6 / 6 / 4**.

The source explains the result. `_WINDOW_STOP` includes `at`, `in` and `for` (`src/query.py:277-278`). `_partners` (`301-312`) actually scans both directions independently, taking up to three non-skipped words on each side. In these primary inputs, `zzdrugzz` stops the scan toward the drug, while `at` immediately stops the other direction. The actual partner list is **empty**, even though `eFluor 450` is explicitly joined later in that same phrase. `_names_reagent` also does not recognize that dye (`246-266`). For ordinary `linked`, `any(...)` over the empty partner list is false (`344-351`), so the joining guard never activates. For an ADC, `conjugated` activates `_item_joined`, but `_joined_beyond_adc` also returns false over the empty list (`355-365`), preserving the ADC exemption at `675-676`. `Engine.explore` then draws the accepted originator at `src/app.py:88-95`.

The two paths are one shared boundary defect, with different observable regression histories. All thirteen strict cases affirm an extra dye attachment. They are neither an ADC merely spelling out its own payload nor a negated modification. Counts are descriptive; the assertions compare complete stored map objects and evidence arrays. The manufacturer's dye/amine-reactivity evidence and source boundaries are documented in the attack findings below. No claim is made that the text uniquely identifies a marketed clinical product.

The controls distinguish the mechanism: removing the intervening setting/site phrase refuses the eFluor case; replacing `at` with `through` refuses it; replacing eFluor with the already recognized ATTO 647N refuses it. Bare drugs, unmodified ADC descriptions and genuine negative controls are evaluated separately. A memory-only change to the stop set demonstrates the causal boundary and its recall tradeoffs; it is not a completeness-tested repair.

## M31-B1 — an early partner-window stop hides an explicit extra dye (P1)

**Hypothesis.** The new clinical/ADC partner allowlists are safe only if an empty window cannot silently stand for a later explicit attachment partner. The code treats `at`, `in`, and `for` as unconditional stops, although these can introduce a conjugation site, reaction setting, or purpose before the partner.

**Primary inherited example:** `trastuzumab linked at lysine residues to eFluor 450` draws **TRASTUZUMAB / CHEMBL1201585**, with the same full map (**13 graph trials**) and QA evidence (**12 / 12 rows**) as bare trastuzumab. The actual `_marked` rest is `['zzdrugzz', 'linked', 'at', 'lysine', 'residues', 'to', 'eFluor', '450']`. `_partners(..., linked)` returns `[]`: the drug marker stops the left scan and `at` stops the right scan. `_item_joined(rest)` returns false, because `_names_reagent` still does not recognize eFluor and `any(...)` over the empty partner list is false.

**Primary new regression:** `trastuzumab emtansine conjugated at lysine residues to eFluor 450` draws **TRASTUZUMAB EMTANSINE / CHEMBL1743082** with its complete **5 / 5 / 5** graph/trial-QA/sponsor-QA result. HEAD^ refuses the same input with no map centre and **0 / 0** QA evidence. Here `_item_joined(rest)` is true (`conjugated` is recognized), but `_joined_beyond_adc(rest)` returns false for the same empty partner window and `_item_reagent(rest)` is false. The ADC exemption therefore accepts an explicitly further-conjugated ADC. Deruxtecan and `in solution` / `for detection` wording show the same regression. The two new modification stems `derivatized` and `functionalized` also reach this exemption; those exact examples were already leaks in HEAD^ because their action words were previously absent.

The failure points are `_WINDOW_STOP` at `src/query.py:277-278`, `_partners` at `301-312`, the linked allowlist at `344-352`, `_joined_beyond_adc` at `355-365`, and the actual marker/exemption expression at `673-677`. Despite the docstring's directional description, `_partners` scans **both sides independently**, taking up to three non-skipped words **per side**; a drug marker stops a scan only when encountered. In these primary inputs, the marker is adjacent to the joining word, so that side is empty. `Engine.explore` consumes the accepted drug at `src/app.py:88-95`. [Numbered excerpts](attacks/source_excerpts.txt), [latest diff](attacks/latest_diff.txt).

**Stage evidence.** For each of the 13 exact inputs, resolver components contain no BLOCKED tier; `_resolver_blocked` is empty; `_qualified` and isotope detection are false; every actual `_marked` return is `None`; the whole-name fallback is `None`; internal/public linkers and both QA entity sets contain no Refused entry. The same checks were performed on the actual trial and sponsor question strings, not inferred from a bare map. Assertions compare complete map objects and complete evidence arrays, not just counts. All 13 have independent original-CLI HTTP corroboration.

**Identity premise.** eFluor 450 is a manufacturer-listed dye used for antibody conjugates ([Thermo Fisher dye guide](https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cell-analysis/flow-cytometry/efluor-organic-dyes.html)). A conjugation site at lysine residues is ordinary antibody-labeling chemistry ([Abcam chemistry guide](https://www.abcam.com/en-us/technical-resources/guides/conjugation-guide/antibody-labeling-chemistries)). These sources ground the interpretation of an explicit extra modification; they do **not** establish a unique marketed trastuzumab-eFluor or ADC-eFluor product. The inputs are synthetic descriptions whose exact product identity is unavailable; returning all evidence for the bare drug is the failure. [Source register and limits](attacks/external_sources.json).

## Causal checks and controls

A memory-only diagnostic removes **only `at`** from `_WINDOW_STOP`; it fixes all six `at`-site strict cases in maps and both QA wrappers, with no other measured change across the 53-case cohort. A broader diagnostic removes `at`, `in`, and `for`; it fixes all 13 strict cases **but also changes two valid clinical controls** (`osimertinib linked to response in 2026` and `osimertinib linked to resistance in EGFR`). Both scenarios restore the exact baseline afterward. This isolates the window stop as a cause and demonstrates why simply deleting stopwords is **not** a validated repair. Original helper source, exact diagnostic code, outputs, and restoration are saved in [counterfactual.json](attacks/counterfactual.json).

Ten explicit-positive control descriptions refuse: the direct eFluor phrases fixed by m30, `through lysine residues` versions, ATTO647N versions, ordinary trastuzumab conjugation, biotinylation and PEGylation. Nineteen negative/bare/clinical controls have accepted maps and public linkers; eighteen also preserve nonempty trial/sponsor QA evidence. The remaining reverse-relation QA regression is reported below, not hidden in map-only controls. Bare ADC descriptions with the descriptor **after** the drug now have the restored **5 / 5** or **6 / 4** QA evidence.

Eight standalone modification descriptions are recorded separately in `assertions.json` as underspecified diagnostics, not required for the P1 result. Trailing `crosslinked` changes from HEAD^ refusal to current acceptance; trailing `derivatized`/`functionalized` remain accepted; leading variants accept maps but now refuse QA. They do not add to the 13 strict explicit-partner count.

## M31-S1 — clinical-relation recall regressions (should fix)

`osimertinib linked to EGFR resistance`, `osimertinib linked to TP53 mutations`, and `osimertinib linked to EGFR mutations` previously returned OSIMERTINIB with **12 / 12** QA evidence. Current code refuses the drug, draws the explicitly named **EGFR / TP53** target, and returns **0 / 0** trial/sponsor evidence. The gene names are outside `_RELATION_WORDS`; `osimertinib linked to drug resistance` remains accepted. These are loss of intended drug recall, not fabricated target edges or an originator leak. Current/HEAD^ and HTTP checks agree. [Extra stages](attacks/extra_results.json).

`resistance linked to osimertinib` still returns an accepted OSIMERTINIB map, satisfying the latest map-only regression test, but both QA wrappers now return refusal and **0 / 0**, previously **12 / 12**. The backward partner window in `Which trials evaluate resistance linked to osimertinib?` includes `resistance`, `evaluate`, `trials`; the question scaffold fails the relation allowlist. The analogous sponsor question fails similarly. [Actual QA stage traces](attacks/new_results.json), [checks](attacks/assertions.json). Map-only acceptance therefore does not establish QA recall.

## Retained prefix-ADC recall limitation (should fix)

`antibody-drug conjugate trastuzumab emtansine` and the deruxtecan variant accept maps, but wrapping either in the same trial/sponsor questions produces **0 / 0** evidence in both HEAD and HEAD^. In current HEAD, the backward partner scan includes scaffold words before the descriptor. HEAD^ has the same observed over-refusal through its older whole-outside-name descriptor check, not through the new partner-window implementation. The behavior is inherited, not a new regression and not the user-waived own-payload case. The suffix-descriptor QA repair is genuine, but does not cover this order. [Paired evidence](attacks/extra_results.json).

820:                     T.canonical_key(tokens[k]) in self.dic["index"]
821:                     or tokens[k].lower() in T.BIOSIMILAR_BRANDS | T.REFORMULATION_NAMES)
822:                     for k in idx)
823:                 if not hit and not named:
824:                     # "liposomal and nanoparticle formulation of doxorubicin": a bare
825:                     # qualifier carries over a listing word to the next item's drug; a
826:                     # product named by itself ("Mvasi and bevacizumab") does not
827:                     dangling = text
828:                     continue
829:                 dangling = None
830:             elif joined and hit:
831:                 text = f"{dangling} ... {text}"
832:                 dangling = None
833:             else:
834:                 dangling = None if not joined else dangling

837:             found.append({"type": "Refused", "id": None, "label": text,
838:                           "matched_text": text,
839:                           "why": "names a distinct product or tracer, not "
840:                                  "the originator molecule"})

842:         matched: set[int] = set()
843:         for size in range(min(5, len(tokens)), 0, -1):
844:             for i in range(len(tokens) - size + 1):
845:                 if (refused | matched) & set(range(i, i + size)):
846:                     continue

853:

855:                 # Several words only make a drug name when the name itself has
856:                 # several words. The key drops spaces, so "is a" read as the
857:                 # abbreviation "isa" (isatuximab) in any question or answer.
858:                 if hits and size > 1 and not re.search(r"[\s\-/]", hits[0]["alias"]):
859:                     hits = None

861:                     did = hits[0]["drug_id"]
862:                     why = self._marked(key, did, tokens, seg, i, i + size)
863:                     if why:
864:                         # the name carries a product suffix or sits beside an isotope:
865:                         # refuse it, never fall back to the bare molecule
866:                         found.append({"type": "Refused", "id": None, "label": why,
867:                                       "matched_text": why,
868:                                       "why": "names a distinct product or tracer, not "
869:                                              "the originator molecule"})
870:                         refused.update(range(i, i + size))
871:                         continue
872:                     if ("Drug", did) not in seen:
873:                         seen.add(("Drug", did))
874:                         found.append({"type": "Drug", "id": did,
875:                                       "label": self.dic["drugs"][did]["name"],
876:                                       "matched_text": window,
877:                                       "matched_alias": hits[0]["alias"]})
878:                     matched.update(range(i, i + size))   # words of a longer name are not read again
879:                     continue
880: 
881:                 if window.lower() in self.targets:
882:                     t = self.targets[window.lower()]
883:                     if ("Target", t["target_id"]) not in seen:
884:                         seen.add(("Target", t["target_id"]))
885:                         found.append({"type": "Target", "id": t["target_id"],
886:                                       "label": t["symbol"], "matched_text": window})
887:                     matched.update(range(i, i + size))   # words of a longer name are not read again
888:                     continue

900:                     continue
901:

+"""Independent HTTP corroboration; production is read-only, outputs stay in m32."""
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+import time
+import urllib.error
+import urllib.request
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+BASE = 'http://127.0.0.1:8932'
+
+def digest(path):
+    h = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open('rb') as f:
+        for block in iter(lambda: f.read(1024 * 1024), b''):
+            h.update(block)
+    return h.hexdigest()
+
+def snapshot():
+    tracked = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'ls-files', '-z'], cwd=ROOT).decode().split('\0')
+    paths = [p for p in tracked if p and not p.startswith('audit_evidence')]
+    paths += ['data/processed/oncokg.sqlite', 'data/processed/resolved.json']
+    return {p: digest(ROOT / p) for p in sorted(set(paths)) if (ROOT / p).is_file()}
+
+def post(text, route='/api/explore', **extra):
+    data = json.dumps({'text': text, **extra}).encode()
+    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + route, data=data, headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'})
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    try:
+        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=90) as response:
+            status, body = response.status, response.read()
+    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
+        status, body = e.code, e.read()
+    return {'text': text, 'route': route, 'status': status,
+            'seconds': time.perf_counter() - start, 'body': json.loads(body)}
+
+def main():
+    before = snapshot()
+    (OUT / 'root_before_hashes.json').write_text(json.dumps(before, indent=2), encoding='utf-8')
+    page = urllib.request.urlopen(BASE + '/', timeout=30).read()
+    page_exact = page == (ROOT / 'web/try.html').read_bytes()
+    cases = [
+        'trastuzumab', 'trastu$zumab', 'trastu+zumab', 'trastu=zumab',
+        'AstraZeneca', 'AstraZeneca +', 'Merck & Co', 'Merck + Co', 'Roche', 'Roche $',
+        'Tarceva', 'Tarceva™', 'Tarceva®', 'Tarceva©',
+        'osimertinib, Mvasi', 'osimertinib EGFR',
+        'trastuzumab linked at lysine residues to eFluor 450',
+        'trastuzumab emtansine conjugated at lysine residues to eFluor 450',
+        'b.i.o.similar bevacizumab', 'lip.osomal doxorubicin',
+        'medi4736', '5-fluorouracil', 'DHA paclitaxel', 'EGFR',
+        'chembl1201585', 'ensg00000146648', 'nct00000105',
+        'CHEMBL1201585 +', '', 'x' * 501,
+    ]
+    result = [post(t) for t in cases]
+    (OUT / 'root_http.json').write_text(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding='utf-8')
+    after = snapshot()
+    report = {'page_equals_worktree': page_exact, 'request_count': len(result),
+              'changed_files': [p for p in before if before[p] != after.get(p)],
+              'hashes_after': after,
+              'cases': [{'text': r['text'], 'http': r['status'],
+                         'center': r['body'].get('center', {}).get('id'),
+                         'result_keys': list(r['body'])} for r in result]}
+    (OUT / 'root_confirmation.json').write_text(json.dumps(report, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding='utf-8')
+    print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in report.items() if k != 'hashes_after'}, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

[Counts](contract/cost/repeated_match_instrumentation.json). `_item_has_isotope` remains cached at `src/query.py:368-369`; the interior-symbol scan executes inside that cache. The `_item_joined` LRU also remains capped at 4,096 after 8,193 distinct direct inputs. [New cache bound](contract/cost/joined_instrumentation.json).

### M24 joining-guard rescan cost: NOT FIXED as residual overhead

The guard at `src/query.py:673-676` constructs a cache key from the entire list item with each matched span replaced by a marker. With **`' '.join(f'isa x{i:04d}' for i in range(400))`** (3,999 characters, one list item), each replacement yields a different tuple. The separate direct instrumented pass records **400 misses / 320,000 words / 1,282,000 aggregate characters** processed by `_item_joined`; its wrapped guard time is 1.06382 s out of 2.00823 s total. These counts demonstrate growing rescan work, not merely host timing variation. [Instrumentation](contract/cost/joined_instrumentation.json).

For the same 3,999-character workload, the ABBA workers retain the same accepted entity in HEAD and HEAD^. HEAD / HEAD^ medians-of-worker-medians are **0.81082 / 0.79611 s**, and first-call cold medians are **1.44465 / 1.45523 s**. The original CLI HTTP check completes in **2.00970 s**, queues an EGFR map for **1.92352 s**, and a warm repeat completes in **1.57196 s**, all 200. [ABBA samples](contract/cost/joined_cost.json), [HTTP](contract/cost/isolated_joined_unique_cost_http.json). This is a **should-fix cost observation**, with no timeout or incorrect map proven by the performance tests. The same ABBA suite covers 499-character matched inputs, repeated conjugation descriptions, a conjugation after many aliases, and negated-adverb text; each completes under the existing character caps. Changing acceptance to refusal is recorded where expected and is not presented as a same-semantics speed comparison.

The comparisons replace **only `query.py` from HEAD^** against current other modules and data; the M6/M7 comparison similarly substitutes historical query module `9bd7cb4`. They are not whole historical checkouts or a service guarantee. Production HTTP timings run without tracing wrappers. The shared API lock is `src/app.py:247-263`; 3,999/4,000-character probes use the answer field or direct linking because explore rejects text over 500 chars (`src/app.py:239-243,260`). Size checks precede NFKC expansion (`src/query.py:118,524-528`). `Engine.ask` explicitly passes `use_llm=False` (`src/app.py:180-181`); **no model calls or model cost were incurred by these probes**. All seven owned cost-server lifecycles record port closure and unchanged database hashes. No tracked files were edited.

Reproduction from repository root, with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` and `PYTHONUTF8=1`: run `python -B audit_evidence_claims/m31/contract/cost/run23.py initial`, `python -B audit_evidence_claims/m31/contract/cost/joined_cost.py instrument`, `python -B audit_evidence_claims/m31/contract/cost/run23.py quiet`, `python -B audit_evidence_claims/m31/contract/cost/run_extra.py`, then `python -B audit_evidence_claims/m31/contract/cost/build_summary.py`. The recorded execution context, rather than these commands alone, determines whether a timing window overlapped other work.

## M31-C1 — new cold-cache repeated-alias cost (should fix)

The marker at `src/query.py:673-674` makes an otherwise identical repeated-alias item have a different `_item_joined` cache key for each matched position. For **`' '.join(['isa']*1000)`** (3,999 characters), the previous query module has **1 miss / 999 body words / 2,997 token characters**; HEAD has **1,000 misses / 1,000,000 body words / 3,005,000 token characters** (token character counts exclude spaces). The returned ISATUXIMAB entity is identical. At the map-sized **125 repeats / 499 characters**, misses increase **1 to 125** and processed body words **124 to 15,625**. Counts come from the cached function body, so cache hits are not miscounted as repeated work. Every hook is restored. [Body instrumentation](contract/cost/marker_instrumentation.json), [instrumentation code](contract/cost/marker_instrumentation.py).

Eight ABBA workers provide 24 samples with all relevant resolver/refusal caches cleared before every call; graph construction is excluded. These timings measure linking, not end-to-end request latency. The comparison substitutes only `query.py` from HEAD^ against current other modules/data. The audit's primary timing window was coordinated, but unrelated host load is uncontrolled. [Samples](contract/cost/marker_cold_cost.json), [context](contract/cost/execution_context.json).

|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `' '.join(['isa']*125)` | 499 chars; map/direct | 0.08425 s | 0.04935 s | 1.71x |
| `' '.join(['isa']*1000)` | 3999 chars; `/api/check` answer/direct; map cap is 500 | 3.37593 s | 1.23769 s | 2.73x |

The original current CLI reproduction, `POST /api/check` with `text="EGFR"` and the 3,999-character repeated-isa `answer`, returns HTTP 200 in **4.76361 s**, holds the shared engine lock long enough that a queued EGFR map completes in **4.69251 s**, and its warm repeat completes in **3.32902 s**. [HTTP](contract/cost/isolated_repeated_match_cost_http.json). This input uses the answer field's 4,000-character cap; `POST /api/explore` caps text at 500 (`src/app.py:239-243,260`). The lock encloses API work at `src/app.py:247-263`.

The inherited three-call ABBA experiment mixes one cold and two warm calls: its HEAD/HEAD^ medians-of-worker-medians are **1.62819 / 1.45113 s**. It does not measure cold-cache behavior and is retained separately from the new all-cold comparison. No timeout or wrong map is proven by these cost tests; this is a measured regression and a should-fix item, not a relation-identity blocker. The exact new marker placement and the cache-body counts distinguish the new work from older repeated-match overhead.

---run23.py---
"""Re-run inspected original cost scripts, with all outputs under this directory."""
from pathlib import Path
import datetime, json, os, shutil, subprocess, sys, time

OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = OUT.parents[3]
mode = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'initial'
env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE='1', PYTHONUTF8='1',
           PYTHONIOENCODING='utf-8', TEMP=str(OUT/'tmp'), TMP=str(OUT/'tmp'),
           TMPDIR=str(OUT/'tmp'))
names = {
    'initial': ['run_perf_current.py', 'cost_stress.py', 'unique_piece_cost.py',
                'cache_boundary_http.py', 'cache_bound_instrumentation.py'],
    'quiet': ['normalization_cost.py', 'perf_check_http.py', 'fresh_cost.py',
              'unique_cost_http.py', 'unicode_cost_http.py', 'repeated_match_followup.py'],
}[mode]
if mode == 'quiet':
    prior = OUT/'contended'
    prior.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    for pattern in ('*.json', '*.txt'):
        for p in OUT.glob(pattern):
            if not p.name.startswith('execution_quiet'):
                shutil.copy2(p, prior/p.name)
context = json.loads((OUT/'execution_context.json').read_text(encoding='utf8'))
context[mode+'_actual_start_utc'] = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()
(OUT/'execution_context.json').write_text(json.dumps(context, indent=2), encoding='utf8')
rows = []
for name in names:
    start = time.perf_counter()
    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', str(OUT/name)], cwd=ROOT, env=env,
                       capture_output=True, timeout=300)
    (OUT/(name+'.stdout.txt')).write_bytes(p.stdout+p.stderr)
    row = {'script':name, 'exit_code':p.returncode, 'seconds':time.perf_counter()-start}
    rows.append(row)
    (OUT/('execution_'+mode+'.json')).write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2), encoding='utf8')
    print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)
    if p.returncode:
        raise SystemExit(p.returncode)
context[mode+'_finish_utc'] = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()
(OUT/'execution_context.json').write_text(json.dumps(context, indent=2), encoding='utf8')

---perf_probe.py---
"""Bounded subprocess benchmarks; writes confined to m5 and never calls a model."""

import json

import os

from pathlib import Path

import subprocess

import sys

import time

import types



OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

ROOT = OUT.parents[3]

sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / 'src'))



if len(sys.argv) > 1:

    import query

    import textrules as T

    mode, kind, size = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])

    module = query

    if mode == 'm4':

        module = types.ModuleType('perf_m4_query')

        module.__file__ = str(ROOT / 'src/query.py')

        sys.modules[module.__name__] = module

        code = subprocess.run(['git', 'show', 'bf436c6:src/query.py'], cwd=ROOT,

                              capture_output=True, check=True).stdout.decode('utf-8')

        exec(compile(code, module.__file__, 'exec'), module.__dict__)

    kg = module.OncoKG()

    kg.conn.execute('PRAGMA query_only=ON')

    text = {'plain': ' '.join(['x'] * size),

            'drug': ' '.join(['x'] * size + ['osimertinib']),

            'split': ';'.join(['x'] * size),

            'single': 'x' * size,

            'late_qualifier': ' '.join(['x'] * size + ['biosimilar', 'bevacizumab'])}[kind]

    calls = {'is_distinct_product': 0, 'is_radiotracer': 0, 'characters': 0}

    for name in ['is_distinct_product', 'is_radiotracer']:

        original = getattr(T, name)

        def wrapped(value, name=name, original=original):

            calls[name] += 1

            calls['characters'] += len(value)

            return original(value)

        setattr(T, name, wrapped)

    start = time.perf_counter()

    entities = kg.link_entities(text)

    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start

    kg.conn.close()

    print(json.dumps({'mode': mode, 'kind': kind, 'size': size, 'characters': len(text),

                     'seconds': elapsed, 'calls': calls, 'entities': entities}))

else:

    env = {**os.environ, 'PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE': '1', 'PYTHONUTF8': '1',

           'PYTHONIOENCODING': 'utf-8', 'TEMP': str(OUT / 'tmp'),

           'TMP': str(OUT / 'tmp'), 'TMPDIR': str(OUT / 'tmp')}

    cases = [('plain', n) for n in [50, 100, 200, 250, 500, 1000]]

    cases += [('drug', 244), ('split', 250), ('single', 500), ('late_qualifier', 235)]

    rows = []

    for kind, size in cases:

        for mode in ['m4', 'HEAD']:

            try:

                proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', __file__, mode, kind, str(size)],

                                      cwd=ROOT, env=env, capture_output=True, timeout=20)

                row = json.loads(proc.stdout) if proc.returncode == 0 else {

                    'mode': mode, 'kind': kind, 'size': size, 'error': proc.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace')}

            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:

                row = {'mode': mode, 'kind': kind, 'size': size, 'timeout_seconds': 20}

            rows.append(row)

            (OUT / 'perf_results.json').write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2), encoding='utf-8')

            print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)

          ('many_joiners',' and '.join(['x']*666))]

    times=[]

    for _ in range(3):

    start=time.perf_counter(); result=e.check('EGFR',value); check=time.perf_counter()-start

    rows.append({'name':name,'text':value,'characters':len(value),'link_seconds':times,

from pathlib import Path
import functools,json,subprocess,sys,time,types
OUT=Path(__file__).resolve().parent;ROOT=OUT.parents[3]
sys.path.insert(0,str(ROOT/'src'))
def module(ref):
    import query
    if ref=='HEAD':return query
    name='marker_previous_query';m=types.ModuleType(name);m.__file__=str(ROOT/'src/query.py');sys.modules[name]=m
    exec(compile(subprocess.check_output(['git','show',f'{ref}:src/query.py'],cwd=ROOT).decode('utf8'),m.__file__,'exec'),m.__dict__)
    return m
rows=[]
for ref in ('HEAD^','HEAD'):
    q=module(ref)
    for n in (125,1000):
        text=' '.join(['isa']*n);kg=q.OncoKG();kg.conn.execute('PRAGMA query_only=ON')
        original=q._item_joined;original.cache_clear()
        counts={'outer_calls':0,'body_calls':0,'body_words':0,'body_characters':0,'body_seconds':0.0}
        raw=original.__wrapped__
        @functools.lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
        def counted_body(words):
            counts['body_calls']+=1;counts['body_words']+=len(words);counts['body_characters']+=sum(map(len,words));start=time.perf_counter()
            value=raw(words);counts['body_seconds']+=time.perf_counter()-start;return value
        def outer(words):
            counts['outer_calls']+=1;return counted_body(words)
        q._item_joined=outer
        try:
            start=time.perf_counter();entities=kg.link_entities(text);elapsed=time.perf_counter()-start
            row={'ref':ref,'input':text,'characters':len(text),'matches':n,'counts':dict(counts),'cache':counted_body.cache_info()._asdict(),'instrumented_seconds':elapsed,'entities':entities}
        finally:q._item_joined=original;kg.conn.close()
        assert q._item_joined is original
        rows.append(row)
for n in (125,1000):
    a,b=[r for r in rows if r['matches']==n]
    assert a['entities']==b['entities']
    assert a['cache']['misses']==1 and b['cache']['misses']==n
(OUT/'marker_instrumentation.json').write_text(json.dumps({'setup':'Count raw cached function body work through equivalent lru_cache, restored after each call. Instrumented elapsed times are not service latency. Same current database/other modules; only query.py differs.','rows':rows},indent=2),encoding='utf8')

---perf_check_http.py---
"""Bounded probe of the answer field passed back into the new linker."""

import concurrent.futures

import hashlib

import json

import os

from pathlib import Path

import socket

import subprocess

import sys

import time

import urllib.error

import urllib.request



OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

ROOT = OUT.parents[3]

BASE = 'http://127.0.0.1:14260'

DB = ROOT / 'data/processed/oncokg.sqlite'



def post(path, payload, timeout):

    started = time.perf_counter()

    try:

        req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + path, data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),

                                     headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'})

        try:

            response = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout)

        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:

            response = error

        return {'status': response.status, 'body': json.loads(response.read()),

                'seconds': time.perf_counter()-started}

    except TimeoutError:

        return {'timeout_seconds': timeout, 'seconds': time.perf_counter()-started}



with socket.socket() as sock:

    assert sock.connect_ex(('127.0.0.1', 14260)) != 0

before = hashlib.sha256(DB.read_bytes()).hexdigest()

env = {**os.environ, 'PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE': '1', 'PYTHONUTF8': '1'}

with (OUT / 'perf_check_server.txt').open('w', encoding='utf8') as log:

    proc = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '-B', '-u', 'src/app.py', '14260'], cwd=ROOT,

        env=env, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,

        creationflags=getattr(subprocess, 'CREATE_NO_WINDOW', 0))

    try:

        for _ in range(100):

            assert proc.poll() is None

            try:

                urllib.request.urlopen(BASE, timeout=1).read()

                break

            except OSError:

                time.sleep(.1)

        else:

            raise RuntimeError('server unavailable')

        normal = post('/api/explore', {'text':'EGFR'}, 5)

        small = post('/api/check', {'text':'EGFR', 'answer':' '.join(['x']*100)}, 5)

        payload = {'text':'EGFR', 'answer':' '.join(['x']*500)}

        slow = post('/api/check', payload, 5)

        started = time.perf_counter()

        get = urllib.request.urlopen(BASE, timeout=2)

        get.read()

        live_get = {'status': get.status, 'seconds': time.perf_counter()-started}

        follower = post('/api/explore', {'text':'EGFR'}, 2)

        output = {'normal_before': normal, 'small_check_199_characters': small,

                  'slow_check_input': payload, 'slow_check_999_characters': slow,

                  'get_while_check_running': live_get, 'normal_after_check_timeout': follower,

                  'limitation':'Client timeouts bound the observation; not a completed latency or permanent deadlock claim.'}

        (OUT / 'perf_check_http.json').write_text(json.dumps(output, indent=2), encoding='utf8')

        print(json.dumps({k: ({x:y for x,y in v.items() if x!='body'} if isinstance(v,dict) else v)

                          for k,v in output.items() if k!='slow_check_input'}))

    finally:

        proc.terminate()

        proc.wait(timeout=10)

        with socket.socket() as sock:

            closed = sock.connect_ex(('127.0.0.1', 14260)) != 0

        after = hashlib.sha256(DB.read_bytes()).hexdigest()

        (OUT / 'perf_check_lifecycle.json').write_text(json.dumps({'pid':proc.pid, 'port':14260,

            'port_closed':closed,'database_unchanged':before==after,'server_exit':proc.returncode},indent=2),encoding='utf8')

        assert closed and before==after



---cache_boundary_http.py---
"""Reach the 4097-entry resolver-cache boundary through legal original-CLI requests."""

from pathlib import Path

import hashlib,json,os,socket,subprocess,sys,time,urllib.request,urllib.error

OUT=Path(__file__).resolve().parent;ROOT=OUT.parents[3];PORT=14260;BASE=f'http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}'

env={**os.environ,'PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE':'1','PYTHONIOENCODING':'utf-8','TEMP':str(OUT/'tmp'),'TMP':str(OUT/'tmp'),'TMPDIR':str(OUT/'tmp')}

def post(text):

 t=time.perf_counter();req=urllib.request.Request(BASE+'/api/explore',json.dumps({'text':text}).encode(),{'Content-Type':'application/json'})

 try:r=urllib.request.urlopen(req,timeout=20)

 except urllib.error.HTTPError as ex:r=ex

 with r:body=json.load(r);status=r.status

 return {'input':text,'characters':len(text),'status':status,'seconds':time.perf_counter()-t,'center':body.get('center'),'error':body.get('error'),'body':body if status!=200 else None}

sock=socket.socket();sock.bind(('127.0.0.1',PORT));sock.close()

before=hashlib.sha256((ROOT/'data/processed/oncokg.sqlite').read_bytes()).hexdigest()

with (OUT/'cache_boundary_server.txt').open('w',encoding='utf8') as log:

 p=subprocess.Popen([sys.executable,'-B','-u','src/app.py',str(PORT)],cwd=ROOT,env=env,stdout=log,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,creationflags=getattr(subprocess,'CREATE_NO_WINDOW',0));rows=[]

 try:

  for _ in range(100):

   if p.poll() is not None:raise RuntimeError('server exit')

   try:urllib.request.urlopen(BASE,timeout=1).read();break

   except OSError:time.sleep(.1)

  else:raise RuntimeError('server startup timeout')

  pieces=[f'isa x{i:04d}' for i in range(4096)]

  for offset in range(0,len(pieces),50):

   text=';'.join(pieces[offset:offset+50]);assert len(text)<=500

   row=post(text);row['filled_distinct_pieces']=min(offset+50,4096);rows.append(row)

   if row['status']!=200:break

  boundary=post('osimertinib');retry=post('osimertinib')

  result={'fill_requests':len(rows),'fill_http_200':sum(r['status']==200 for r in rows),'fill':rows,'boundary':boundary,'retry':retry}

  (OUT/'cache_boundary_http.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2,ensure_ascii=False),encoding='utf8')

  print(json.dumps({'fill_requests':len(rows),'filled':rows[-1]['filled_distinct_pieces'],'boundary':boundary,'retry_status':retry['status'],'retry_center':retry['center']},ensure_ascii=False))

 finally:

  p.terminate();p.wait(timeout=10)

  after=hashlib.sha256((ROOT/'data/processed/oncokg.sqlite').read_bytes()).hexdigest()

  with socket.socket() as sock:closed=sock.connect_ex(('127.0.0.1',PORT))!=0

  (OUT/'cache_boundary_lifecycle.json').write_text(json.dumps({'pid':p.pid,'port':PORT,'port_closed':closed,'db_before':before,'db_after':after,'db_unchanged':before==after,'exit':p.returncode},indent=2),encoding='utf8')

  (OUT/'isolated_unique_cost_http.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2,ensure_ascii=False),encoding='utf8');print(json.dumps({k:{'status':v['status'],'seconds':v['seconds']} for k,v in result.items() if isinstance(v,dict)},indent=2))

 finally:

  with socket.socket() as sock:closed=sock.connect_ex(('127.0.0.1',PORT))!=0

+"""Independent HTTP corroboration; production is read-only, outputs stay in m32."""
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+import time
+import urllib.error
+import urllib.request
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+BASE = 'http://127.0.0.1:8932'
+
+def digest(path):
+    h = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open('rb') as f:
+        for block in iter(lambda: f.read(1024 * 1024), b''):
+            h.update(block)
+    return h.hexdigest()
+
+def snapshot():
+    tracked = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'ls-files', '-z'], cwd=ROOT).decode().split('\0')
+    paths = [p for p in tracked if p and not p.startswith('audit_evidence')]
+    paths += ['data/processed/oncokg.sqlite', 'data/processed/resolved.json']
+    return {p: digest(ROOT / p) for p in sorted(set(paths)) if (ROOT / p).is_file()}
+
+def post(text, route='/api/explore', **extra):
+    data = json.dumps({'text': text, **extra}).encode()
+    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + route, data=data, headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'})
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    try:
+        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=90) as response:
+            status, body = response.status, response.read()
+    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
+        status, body = e.code, e.read()
+    return {'text': text, 'route': route, 'status': status,
+            'seconds': time.perf_counter() - start, 'body': json.loads(body)}
+
+def main():
+    before = snapshot()
+    (OUT / 'root_before_hashes.json').write_text(json.dumps(before, indent=2), encoding='utf-8')
+    page = urllib.request.urlopen(BASE + '/', timeout=30).read()
+    page_exact = page == (ROOT / 'web/try.html').read_bytes()
+    cases = [
+        'trastuzumab', 'trastu$zumab', 'trastu+zumab', 'trastu=zumab',
+        'AstraZeneca', 'AstraZeneca +', 'Merck & Co', 'Merck + Co', 'Roche', 'Roche $',
+        'Tarceva', 'Tarceva™', 'Tarceva®', 'Tarceva©',
+        'osimertinib, Mvasi', 'osimertinib EGFR',
+        'trastuzumab linked at lysine residues to eFluor 450',
+        'trastuzumab emtansine conjugated at lysine residues to eFluor 450',
+        'b.i.o.similar bevacizumab', 'lip.osomal doxorubicin',
+        'medi4736', '5-fluorouracil', 'DHA paclitaxel', 'EGFR',
+        'chembl1201585', 'ensg00000146648', 'nct00000105',
+        'CHEMBL1201585 +', '', 'x' * 501,
+    ]
+    result = [post(t) for t in cases]
+    (OUT / 'root_http.json').write_text(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding='utf-8')
+    after = snapshot()
+    report = {'page_equals_worktree': page_exact, 'request_count': len(result),
+              'changed_files': [p for p in before if before[p] != after.get(p)],
+              'hashes_after': after,
+              'cases': [{'text': r['text'], 'http': r['status'],
+                         'center': r['body'].get('center', {}).get('id'),
+                         'result_keys': list(r['body'])} for r in result]}
+    (OUT / 'root_confirmation.json').write_text(json.dumps(report, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding='utf-8')
+    print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in report.items() if k != 'hashes_after'}, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

Reviewed HEAD `b21da2b29c3333af2075433043e32eeb2bb8af21`, parent `4493fe0f21ad7615594be5d7715b1b90de2a1ed6`. All mutations in these probes were confined to private SQLite `:memory:` copies. All scratch files are under `m32/attacks`. Actual server exercised: `http://127.0.0.1:8932`.

## Code blocker A: the full-input check compares the input to its own linker window

Requirements: P32-1 and approval bar, whole input must be one stored name, significant letters/digits/symbols preserved. Locations: `src/app.py:111-115`, `src/app.py:247-259`, `src/query.py:872-877`, `src/textrules.py:340-347`.

The linker looks up a lossy canonical key, then returns the original candidate window as `matched_text`. `explore` compares `_sig(matched_text)` to `_sig(input)`, proving only that the linker window covers the input. It does not prove equality to a stored alias. `_plain` admits ASCII symbols and Latin letters that the canonical key removes. No alias `trastu$zumab` or `trastuzumabß` exists, but both draw trastuzumab.

HTTP 200 reproductions (`http_identity.json`):

## Code blocker B: the company fallback bypasses whole-signature equality

Requirement P32-4 says a symbol dropped by the key must still block the input. Actual HEAD contains `_plain`, not the `_latin` described in the round brief. `src/app.py:120-122` directly looks up `canonical_key(text)` whenever `_plain(text)` is true; it does not compare a significant signature to any stored company key/name.

HTTP 200 (`http_identity.json`): `AstraZeneca +` -> ORG:astrazeneca; `Merck + Co` -> ORG:merckco, label `Merck & Co`; `Pfizer$` and `Pfi+zer` -> ORG:pfizer; `Roche $` -> ORG:roche. The last input also bypasses the normal Roche ambiguity: the drug window fails whole-name equality, while the company fallback succeeds. `Merck & Co` itself remains a valid positive control. `Merck ☢ Co` is rejected, demonstrating that the current character-class gate protects only some symbols.

## Code blocker C: same stored name under punctuation/spacing still draws one node

Requirements P32-3 and page `web/try.html:54`, `:217-218`: same-name nodes require the reader's choice; punctuation/spacing do not count. | `ABT-510`, `ABT 510` | abt510 | CHEMBL386115 and CHEMBL262489 | Each spelling draws its own preferred-name node |
